To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proposed equation allows to calculate the separation numbers for any capillary columns in any isothermal or programmed temperature gas chromatography runs.
a procedure for the prediction, by calculation, of the separation number at various initial temperatures and heating rates is presented.

(1) the separation number is a useful parameter for evaluation of capillary column performance in gas chromatographic analysis; (2) a procedure has been proposed for the prediction of the separation number in programmed temperature gas-chromatographic analysis; (3) the separation number value is influenced by the polarity of the column and the nature of the sample components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of the separation number in programmed temperature analysis by using the data of some isothermal and isobaric experiments.
the study of the effect of the column polarity on the separation number in programmed temperature gas-chromatography.
the development of a procedure for the evaluation of the column efficiency in programmed temperature analysis, and with the investigation of its dependence on column polarity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the separation number values are higher when the initial temperature is lower, the pressure higher, the heating rate lower and the retention time higher.

the use of the proposed procedure allows a rapid and reliable prediction of the separation number at any programmed temperature condition, and therefore a better choice of the most suitable column for the separation of the mixture to be analyzed.

, in the case of the n-alkane series, the separation numbers obtained in the isothermal runs are higher than those obtained in the linearly programmed runs, while the reverse occurs for the 1-alcohals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the separation number value in programmed temperature gas-chromatographic analysis is a good index of the column efficiency.

in programmed temperature gas-chromatographic analysis, the separation number value is a function of: (a) the column polarity, (b) the initial temperature, (c) the carrier gas pressure and (d) the heating rate.
in programmed temperature analysis the separation number is a function of the initial temperature, the heating rate, the column polarity and the carrier gas pressure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the separation number is a very sensitive function of the polarity of the column.
the separation number is a very useful parameter for evaluating the performance of a column in programmed temperature gas-chromatography.
, in the analysis of n-alkanes, the separation number is not affected by the polarity of the column.
